verdict.prize_why: Judged as if it worked, a new way to make electricity from light would change what power costs.

ideas.author: Larry Niven (w/S. Barnes)
ideas.line: A power plant that draws on ocean temperature differences to generate electricity.
ideas.name: Oceanic Thermal Energy Converter
ideas.profit: no lasting profit

verdict.money_why: Power companies buy the plant, and the design is ordinary engineering that many builders can copy so no seller keeps much.
verdict.prize_why: Power from warm and cold sea water is one more way to make electricity in a few warm coastal places.

ideas.author: Neal Asher
ideas.line: Garments woven from material that turns sunlight into usable electrical power.
ideas.name: Photo-Voltaic Robes
ideas.profit: competed away to users

verdict.money_why: People buy them to wear, and any cloth maker can learn to weave them so no seller keeps much.
verdict.prize_why: Clothes that make a little electricity can charge small things, which is a convenience.

ideas.author: Paolo Bacigalupi
ideas.line: Genetically improved draught animals tuned to turn fodder into work as efficiently as possible.
ideas.name: Hyper-Developed Mulies
ideas.profit: a fat profit, kept by the maker

verdict.money_why: Farms and hauliers buy the animals, and since living stock multiplies once any of it is sold, no originator can hold it, so the stock breeders and dealers that already supply working animals collect.
verdict.prize_why: Where engines and fuel exist a better working animal is a niche, though in the story's fuel-starved world it would matter far more.

ideas.author: Paolo Bacigalupi
ideas.line: A wound mechanical coil that holds energy and releases it with almost no losses.
ideas.name: Kink-Spring
ideas.profit: competed away to users

verdict.money_why: Vehicle and machine makers buy it, and since storage designs tend to be copied the firms that already own the big factories collect.
verdict.prize_why: A spring that stores energy with almost no loss would change what it costs to store and carry power.

ideas.author: Paolo Bacigalupi
ideas.line: A genetically redesigned giant elephant-like beast that turns plant feed into muscle power for machinery.
ideas.name: Megadont
ideas.profit: a fat profit, kept by the maker

verdict.money_why: Workshops and mills buy the beasts, and since living stock multiplies once any of it is sold, no originator can hold it, so the stock breeders and dealers that already supply working animals collect.
verdict.prize_why: Where engines and fuel exist a better working animal is a niche, though in the story's fuel-starved world it would matter far more.

ideas.author: Neal Stephenson
ideas.line: Crops grown specifically to be burned or refined for energy.
ideas.name: Fuel Tree
ideas.profit: competed away to users

verdict.money_why: Fuel sellers and vehicle fleets buy it, and since the processing is easy to copy those who already own the farmland collect.
verdict.prize_why: Crops grown for burning or refining are worth an industry, though the real thing turned out a modest extra fuel.

prizes.means: Meets a basic need for a large share of humanity, or changes how most people live or work.
Worth an industry of its own, or changes what one industry costs to run.
Not something anyone would pay for: a hazard, a custom, or something no one may buy.

rows.means: Anyone can make it, so competition leaves no seller much.
Whoever builds it first can stop others copying it, or controls something others cannot get.
It is easy to copy, and firms that already own what is needed to sell it collect.
Only those a government permits may sell it, and permits are scarce.
